# PLUCK — what a duck can become

**As-built.** Every table is read straight out of `Faultline.Core`, so this is what the game
does today, not what the design doc intends. Where the two differ, `DECISIONS.md` says why.

Written to be reviewed: each section ends with **what is thin**, counted rather than felt.

## How progression works

A run is a walk across an act's columns. Four things can change a duck, and they are
deliberately different in kind:

| Where | When | What it hands over | Who chooses |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Camp** | after every won combat node | one card per player | each player, from their own table |
| **Still Pond** | its own node | hit points back, or the Forge | the party |
| **Event** | its own node | a body trade, priced in HP | each duck's owner |
| **Destination** | gilt-marked nodes | a permanent legendary | the party |

**The camp is two tables, one pick each** — each table addressed to that player's ducks, and
the node does not resolve until both are spent. Card tiers are drawn on weights rather than
branches, and the weights differ by lane:

| Source | Common | Uncommon | Rare |
|---|---|---|---|
| SafeCamp | 60 | 35 | 5 |
| HungryCamp | 35 | 50 | 15 |

Weights, not percentages: a tier whose pool is empty contributes nothing, so a table is
never short a card because the dice asked for a tier that has run out.

**Nothing in the camp pool is Rare.** Every Rare the build ships is a destination legendary —
that is the tier ladder and the reward-source split being the same statement.

**Kit surgery is the shape of a build.** A duck holds a fixed number of ability slots and
Pluck-spender slots; learning past a full slot means *replacing*, and the card names what it
replaces. A slot count is per class, not per duck:

| Class | Ability slots | Pluck slots | Starts with |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vanguard | 3 | 1 | 2 abilities, 1 spender(s) |
| Archer | 3 | 1 | 2 abilities, 1 spender(s) |
| Fisher | 3 | 1 | 2 abilities, 1 spender(s) |
| Wardbearer | 4 | 1 | 3 abilities, 1 spender(s) |

### What is thin

- **The Molt is not built.** Clearing an act grants nothing; the between-runs layer where
  permanence was supposed to live does not exist yet, so every run starts from the same duck.
- **Two reward sources are tuned, not three.** `RarityOdds` has a row for the safe camp and
  the hungry camp. The Forge has no row.
- **The odds themselves are unplaytested** — locked ladder, unlocked numbers.

### What is thin

- **Vanguard** knows 3 abilities, holds 2 of 3 slots — 1 learnable.
- **Archer** knows 2 abilities, holds 2 of 3 slots — and there is **nothing it could learn**, so its ability slots can only ever be filled the way they start.
- **Fisher** knows 3 abilities, holds 2 of 3 slots — 1 learnable.
- **Wardbearer** knows 4 abilities, holds 3 of 4 slots — 1 learnable.

**There are 3 learnable abilities in the whole game** — at most one per class, and none at all for the Archer. Kit surgery's Learn/Replace is built; for abilities it has one card per duck to act on, and then it is finished for the run.

## Techniques — the v2 camp pool

The only camp category that carries a rarity and offer-validity tags of its own. Tags are
what the Forge's connector requirement reads.

| Technique | Class | Tier | Tags | On | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Follow-In | Vanguard | Common | Traffic | Bull Rush | After the target is pushed at least 1, he may enter the tile it left. |
| Rattling Impact | Vanguard | Uncommon | Impact · Relay | Bull Rush | The first enemy he collides each round is Rattled: the other flock's next displacement of it gains +1 distance and consumes it. |
| Crossing Shot | Archer | Uncommon | Relay | Archer's basic attack | Once per round, when the other flock displaces an enemy through her range-2–3 firing line, deal 2. The initiating preview shows the shot. |
| Spotter | Archer | Common | Relay | Archer's basic attack | She ignores minimum range against an enemy adjacent to the other flock's duck. |
| Hand-Off | Fisher | Uncommon | Relay | Reel | A displacement ending adjacent to the other flock's duck gives that duck's next basic attack on the target Push 1. |
| Short Line | Fisher | Common | Control | Reel | Choose any legal stopping tile on the drag path. Collisions and hazards still stop it earlier. |
| Shelter Step | Wardbearer | Uncommon | Relay · Guard | Guard Stance | If a redirect moves him, the protected duck banks a free step into the tile he left. |
| Stored Force | Wardbearer | Common | Impact · Guard | Spear Thrust | Each tile of hostile displacement his resistance cancels stores 1 Force (max 2); his next tip-tile Spear hit may spend it as a push. |

### What is thin

- **Traffic has one card.** A tag the Forge can ask for and the pool cannot answer is a connector requirement that cannot be met.
- **Control has one card.** A tag the Forge can ask for and the pool cannot answer is a connector requirement that cannot be met.
- **Finish has nothing.** A tag the Forge can ask for and the pool cannot answer is a connector requirement that cannot be met.

### What is thin

- **Mods are the deepest pool by far** — 32 of the camp's 61 cards. Every other category is single digits per class.

  - Fisher: 9

- **Thinnest hosts:** Interpose (2) · Wrecking Weight (3) · Cast (3). A duck holding one of these sees the same handful every camp.

## Items — the pocket

**One pocket per duck.** Use is 0 AP, free-timing inside that duck's own activation, and
one-shot. A pocket already carrying something is a pocket that must be spent before it can
be refilled, which is what makes an item a decision rather than a stat.

| Item | Aim | What it does | In the camp pool |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dried Minnow | None | Gain 2 Pluck now. | yes |
| Bramble Salve | None | Heal 3, never past your maximum. | yes |
| Old Rope | UnitAndTile | Rescue an adjacent clinger as a free action. | yes |
| Duck Feather Charm | None | Refill Footing 1. | yes |
| Crate of Debris | Tile | Place debris on an adjacent open tile. | yes |
| Greased Feather | None | Your next displacement gains 1 distance. | yes |
| Chalk Mark | Unit | Mark an enemy: the other flock's next displacement of it gains 1 distance. | yes |
| Thorn Pouch | Tile | Grow brambles on an adjacent open tile until the end of the round. | yes |
| Split Reed | Unit | Offer an adjacent allied duck a swap of places. Its owner accepts or does not. | yes |
| Signal Whistle | TwoUnits | Swap the activation order of two enemies that have not acted. Intents unchanged. | yes |

### What is thin

- **No legendary consumable is built.** The Sunken Cache's mark is typed, named and deliberately unpayable, so it draws no gilt edge and hands over nothing.

## Legendaries — destinations only

Never in a camp. A legendary comes from a gilt-marked node, the Molt, or a Strait bargain,
and a gilt edge means one is **literally there** — promise, not probability.

| Legendary | Class | Tier | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Follow Through | Vanguard | Rare | After causing a collision, he may move 2 more tiles — free, and the activation waits. |
| Kestrel Step | Archer | Rare | After shooting, she may move 2 more tiles — free, and the activation waits. |
| Deep Roots | Wardbearer | Rare | Guard persists through his next activation, and he may act while it holds. |

### What is thin

- **Vanguard has one legendary** — a pick-1-of-2 that draws for this duck cannot show it two.
- **Archer has one legendary** — a pick-1-of-2 that draws for this duck cannot show it two.
- **Fisher has no legendary** — a pick-1-of-2 that draws for this duck cannot show it two.
- **Wardbearer has one legendary** — a pick-1-of-2 that draws for this duck cannot show it two.

## What one run actually sees

The authored act gives a route **4–6 combat nodes**, so **4–6 camps**. One pick per player
per camp is **4–6 cards each, 8–12 for the party** — out of 61.

**A run meets under a fifth of the pool, and each duck meets far less than that**, because a
card is addressed to one duck and most of the pool is mods hanging off a spender that duck
may not even hold. Two runs on the same seed diverge on the first pick; two runs on different
seeds have almost nothing in common. Whether that reads as variety or as noise is the
question a playtest answers, and it is worth asking before the pool grows.

## Where the room is

Counted, not felt — each of these is a number above rather than an opinion:

1. **Ability learning runs out after one card.** Three classes have exactly one ability they
   do not start with; the Archer has none. So kit surgery's Learn/Replace fires once per duck
   at most, and an Archer's third slot can never be filled by anything. A second learnable
   ability per class is the cheapest change with the largest effect on what a build can be.
2. **The Fisher has no legendary** and the other three have one each — so a pick-1-of-2 at a
   gilt node cannot show two for any duck, and cannot show anything for a Fisher.
3. **Unlocks are three cards and none of them is about a class.** §8.6 calls them
   "one-sentence rule additions per duck"; today they are the same sentence for everyone.
4. **Two technique tags are unanswerable.** The Forge reads tags as a connector requirement;
   Finish has no card at all and Traffic and Control have one each.
5. **Mods are 32 of 61 cards** — over half the camp is one category, and it is the category
   that tunes a number rather than changing what a duck can do.
6. **The Molt is not built**, so nothing survives a run. Every run starts from the same duck
   and the permanence layer the whole dynasty fiction rests on is absent.
